translations.text: For just as a ship that is well moored on anchors on both sides has no fear of the waves, so you will rebuke this evil agitation
which has come upon the world through wicked spirits and is shaking the faith of many.
And you will treat it with contempt, if your soul is armed with the firmness of these words.
If our mind should ask who existed from the beginning, it says: "the Word." Which word? Could it be this human word, or the word of angels?
For the Apostle indicated that the angels too have their own language, when he said: "If I speak with the tongues of men and of angels."
And again, there are two kinds of "word": one is spoken with the voice and dissolves into the air after it is spoken, and the second is the one that exists within us,
which is in our hearts, the word of thought, understanding and skill. Take care that the fact that these share one name does not lead you astray.
For how could the word of a human being have existed from the beginning, when the human being was the last to receive the beginning of its existence?

For before the human being, the wild beasts and cattle were made, and all the creeping things of the waters and of the dry land, and the birds of the sky, and the sun and the moon and the stars, and the plants, and the earth and the sea and the heavens.
So the word of a human being did not exist from the beginning, and neither did the word of angels exist from the beginning,
for every created thing, having received the beginning of its existence from the Creator, is younger than the ages.
And again, the inner word of the heart is also inferior to the mind and younger than it.
But hear this word in a godly and fitting way, for he was speaking of the Only-begotten and called him "Word," just as a little later he calls him "Light" and "Life" and "Resurrection."
And when you hear "light," do not be drawn toward this visible light; and when you hear "life," do not take it to mean this ordinary life of ours, which the beasts also have.
In the same way, when you hear "Word," be careful that the weakness of your nature does not lead you toward lowly and earthly thoughts.
Instead, look into its meaning: why did he say "Word"? To show that he came forth from the mind. Why is he the Word?
Because he was begotten without passion. Why is he the Word? Because he is the image of the one who begot him and shows him completely in himself.
He is not separated from him, and he is complete in himself. For just as our word expresses the thought of our heart, and what we have conceived in the heart
we utter in speech, and the spoken word is an image of the heart's thought,
for the word comes forth out of the abundance of the heart. Our heart is like a spring, and the word is like the water that rises from that spring.
The stream is as great as what first rose up, and what is revealed is just like what is hidden.

So he said "Word" to show you the Father's begetting without passion, to speak theologically of the Son's perfect being, and to reveal through these words the timeless union of the Son with the Father.
For this word of ours is also an offspring of the mind, begotten without passion, for it is not cut off, nor divided, nor does it flow away,
to whom belong glory and might, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.
